author: P. K. Mishra, Excavation Branch-III, ASI
name_in_asr: Begampur; Daman-khanda (extension of ancient Nalanda Mahavihar)
asr_identification: Begampur and Daman-khanda, 1 km N of the Nalanda ruins (Nalanda district): settlement and Buddhist temple on the periphery of the Mahavihara
evidence: Begampur: terracotta sealing fragment, three lines in Brahmi of c. 7th century, read 'Sri Sakkraditya [kara saka]…, Chaturddisaryya [danaya]…', with a running deer at left. Daman-khanda (NW of the village, 1 km N of the ruins): small dig to trace the extension of the Mahavihara; Buddhist brick temple with stucco as at the Nalanda temples, headless Buddha in a niche, miniature stupas; NBPW, Gupta–post-Gupta and Pala periods.
quote: fragment of sealing with Brahmi script … having a three line inscription “Sri … Sakkraditya [kara saka] … Chaturddisaryya [danaya] … 7th century CE and on its left a running deer … at north-west of the village Daman-khanda … situated 1km north of the ruins of the ancient … excavation was to trace out the extension on
note: The sealing names Śakrāditya, whom Xuanzang makes the founder of the first Nālandā monastery (帝日王), with what looks like 'cāturdiśārya[bhikṣusaṅgha]' (the monks of the four quarters), in 7th-century characters, with a running deer (perhaps a monastic emblem): an inscribed find tying the Śakrāditya tradition to the Nālandā ruins in Xuanzang's century. Supports Mizutani 09.03.01 (agreed) and Cunningham (asr). The report does not mention Xuanzang or discuss the reading; Daman-khanda shows the monastic area ran c. 1 km N of the excavated ruins.
Ghorakatora (near Giriyak) excavation, chalcolithic to Pala; the report does not link it with Xuanzang. The 2013-14 BHU survey puts the Indrasila cave 1 km E of the mound (coded at 785).
Ghorakatora finds (sealings 'Avisi Vaishvani', crowned Buddha bronze); no Xiyu ji place located.

evidence: Second season at Ghaskol Darwaja and Durga Mata Mandir, new trench at Khari Kui; four periods at Ghaskol: pre-Kshatrapa, Kshatrapa, post-Kshatrapa & Maitraka, Rajput (Chavada-Solanki); a 16.80 x 14.05 m building of Period II with chambers along its walls.

author: Y. S. Rawat, Department of Archaeology, Gujarat
asr_identification: Vadnagar (Mehsana): building near the Ghaskol gate, possibly a Buddhist monastery
evidence: The Period II building has chambers arranged like a swastika round a central open square, compared with the plans of Buddhist monasteries in central India (purpose still open); post-Kshatrapa sealings with short Brahmi legends; coins of the Kshatrapas; a stone plaque of the monkey offering honey to the Buddha; a Gandhara-style head.
quote: like a swastika design, wherein the … chambers form the arms of the swastika … special and to some extent comparable to the … ground plan of a few Buddhist monasteries … monastery (or a granary, a waste water … plaque depicting the tale of a monkey … offering honey to Lord Buddha a sand stone
note: First sign of the Buddhist monastery at Vadnagar (called a monastery outright in 2009-10, 749). Xuanzang counts some ten monasteries at Anandapura; Buddhist remains at Vadnagar support Mizutani's 11.09 (disputed) without naming the place. Excavators make no link.

author: Y. S. Rawat, Department of Archaeology, Gujarat
evidence: Trench A-1/I 15 m inside the fortification, 14 m deep, 35 strata, seven periods; a wall of 129 brick courses: lower 76 Kshatrapa and pre-Kshatrapa, upper 53 Maitraka and Rajput; town plan unchanged from the early centuries CE to the 13th century; Kumarapala's inscription on repairing the fort.
quote: Kshatrapa and pre-Kshatrapa periods, … whereas the upper 53 courses represent two … made during the Maitraka and Rajput … town planning of Vadnagar from the early … centuries of Christian era did not deviate … much until 13th century CE.
note: A continuously planned fortified town through the Maitraka period, consistent with Mizutani's Anandapura = Vadnagar (11.09, disputed); no Xuanzang link in the report.

author: D. N. Dimri, ASI
asr_identification: Ahichchhatra, 11 km N of Aonla (Bareilly), between the Ramganga and Ghagan
evidence: Recalls Hiuen Tsang's visit and account, Cunningham's relic casket in the solid brick wall of the stupa, Dikshit's nine periods (3rd c. BCE–1100 CE) with Temples 1–2, Banerjee's OCP–medieval sequence; new dig to check a GPR survey (IIT Kanpur) and the settlement outside the W fortification: Kushana copper and pottery workshop on ACT-V; later Gupta/post-Gupta structures on ACT-VA and ACT-IV; a coin of the Panchala king Achyu.
quote: Panchala. Chinese Traveller Hiuen Tsang … visited Ahichchhatra in 7th Century CE and … has left behind vivid account of the site … The earlier excavations by Cunningham had … resulted in the unearthing of a relic casket in … the solid brick wall of the stupa; by Rai
note: Ahichchhatra = Xuanzang's Ahicchattra assumed, as Mizutani 04.13 (agreed) and Cunningham (asr). The new later-Gupta/post-Gupta structures W of the fort are of about Xuanzang's time but are not tied to his monasteries or the nāga-tank stupa (04.13.x1).

note: Continuation of 736. A later-Gupta temple just outside the city fits Xuanzang's deva temples at Ahicchattra in a general way; no identification argued. Consistent with Mizutani 04.13.

author: B. R. Mani and Praveen Kumar Mishra, Lucknow Circle, ASI; Ahichhatra: Bhuvan Vikrama, Excavation Branch-IV, ASI
name_in_asr: Piprahwa, Ganwaria and Tola Salargarh; Ahichhatra
asr_identification: Piprahwa, Ganwaria and Tola Salargarh (Siddharthnagar); Ahichhatra (Bareilly)
evidence: Ahichhatra (end of report): continuous settlement OCP to 12th century CE; sequence OCP, formative PGW, PGW, Mitra Panchala, Gupta. Piprahwa group: fresh vertical excavation, 12 trenches (7 Ganwaria, 3 Piprahwa, 2 Tola Salargarh); an old 1970s trench at Ganwaria reopened for the cultural index; C14 samples. Ganwaria Period I pre-NBPW, Period II NBPW with beads and an agate weight.

note: The report never says Kapilavastu; Piprahwa–Ganwaria = Kapilavastu (the study's identification, from Srivastava's 1971-77 sealings; Mizutani 06.02 has Tilaurakot) is taken for granted and the seasons are for dating, not for the identification. Ahichhatra: occupation through Xuanzang's time, consistent with Mizutani 04.13.

author: B. R. Mani and Praveen Kumar Mishra, Lucknow Circle, ASI
asr_identification: Piprahwa–Ganwaria (Siddharthnagar); Tola Salargarh 1 km NE of Piprahwa
evidence: Ganwaria: Period III Sunga, Period IV Kushana with brick structures and floors, a ritual group of three pots including a bowl with a snake-hood rim (read as the snake in Kasyapa's hermitage), Kushana coins, Naigamesha figurines. Piprahwa: two quadrants NE and N of the stupa found no habitation deposit, only brick-bats in pits sealed by layer 1. Tola Salargarh: Kushana monastery known from the surface; the trenches gave only brick-bats, a Kushana coin and Sunga-Kushana pottery (short occupation, deposit lost to farming). Two trenches between Piprahwa and Ganwaria reached natural soil at c. 2 m. 85 charcoal samples from four periods.
quote: in the hermitage of Mahakasyapa which came … was selected for excavation. As no habitational … deposit was found so far from the excavation … at Piprahwa except some brick bats filling in … Piprahwa and has remains of a monastery … suggested that this site was occupied for a short … Two trenches were laid between Piprahwa … up to depth of about 2m but only natural
note: Kapilavastu (06.02): the new trenches found no new sealings or inscriptions naming Kapilavastu, no habitation N and NE of the Piprahwa stupa, no deposit linking Piprahwa and Ganwaria (natural soil between them), and no period after the Kushana at Ganwaria. So nothing new for or against the study's Piprahwa–Ganwaria identification, which still rests on the 1970s sealings; the lack of post-Kushana levels fits Xuanzang's long-deserted city but is not evidence for it. Mizutani (Tilaurakot) not discussed.

Lauriya Areraj (East Champaran), K. C. Srivastava, Excavation Branch Patna: a Sunga-Kushana monastery (central courtyard, cells, shrine) E of the Asoka pillar, small structures to the W; dated 1st c. BCE–3rd c. CE; the report places it on the Vaisali–Lumbini route via Kesariya and Lauriya Nandangarh. No Xiyu ji place is identified here and none in the master table sits at Areraj (Kesariya is 07.03.13; Lauriya Nandangarh is Smith's candidate for 06.03.04).

author: Gautam Kumar Lama, Department of Ancient Indian History, Culture and Archaeology, Banaras Hindu University
name_in_asr: Buddhavana (Ayer); Indra Shila cave on Giriyak hill
asr_identification: Ayer (on the Nalanda–Gaya border, 37 km SW of the Nalanda ruins): hill with two natural caverns = Buddhavana; Indrasila cave on the S face of Giriyak hill, 1 km E of the Ghorakatora mound
evidence: Survey of over 100 villages round Nalanda with distances from the ruins (incl. a 'Xuan-Zang Memorial Hall'). Ayer: hill with two natural caverns SW of the village; Buddhist sculptures and a Buddha panel inscribed with the 'Ye dhamma' creed. Ghorakatora: 250 x 200 m mound on the Panchane, pottery from before the 10th c. BCE; the Indrasila cave 1 km E. (The passage itself opens with the end of the Lauriya Areraj report, see 784.)
quote: to Xuan-zang’s description during the … journey from Bodh Gaya to Rajgriha … Buddha stayed at Buddhavana which was … about 10 km west to the Jyeshthivana … (present Jethian) of Rajgriha, so Ayer may … be identified with Buddhavana … Indra Shila cave is located on the southern … face of the Giriyak hill which was … mentioned by Fahien and Xuan-Zang and
note: Ayer = Buddhavana (09.02.01) is new: Mizutani has no accepted identification (Cunningham's Buddhain hill rejected by Majumdar, asr Budhain). The reason is Xuanzang's distance (Yastivana/Jethian about 30 li E of Buddhavana) and the caverns (his stone chamber); no excavation. Check against Xuanzang's 100+ li NE of Kukkutapada. Giriyak/Indrasila as Mizutani 09.03.11 (agreed). The Xuan-zang mentions (pp. 13, 15) lie beyond the indexed lines; coded here.
